[{:db/id 17592186332715 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "2e3acb8a-9c64-589a-b0a1-55d19079df04" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "8\sqrt[3]{(y+11)^{5}}+C" :db/id 17592186330356} {:answer/id #uuid "4a84cb98-9b13-5e1d-b3f0-776b95159569" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{8}{3}\sqrt[3]{(y+11)^{2}}+C" :db/id 17592186330622} {:answer/id #uuid "82c50580-ea5f-5d76-a971-e5772b6896c6" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\sqrt[3]{(y+11)^{8}}+C" :db/id 17592186331107} {:answer/id #uuid "9807ff7c-bea9-5fb1-8910-b8a4f9e1bd42" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{3}{8}\sqrt[3]{(y+11)^{8}}+C" :db/id 17592186331305} {:answer/id #uuid "a1ceaa5d-7317-520f-bbe3-4033344e9924" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "3\sqrt[3]{(y+11)^{8}}+C" :db/id 17592186331405}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186331305} :answer-field/id #uuid "1efac576-99bc-59ee-aebb-307554ed47c3" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332246}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045486} :question/id #uuid "dab90c5a-327c-5636-bfaa-e6da096f9912" :question/math-academy-id "q-49437" :question/problem "Calculate the integral $$
\displaystyle \int \sqrt[3]{(y+11)^{5}}\,\text{d}y.
$$" :question/worked-solution "First, we rewrite the integral as

$$
\int (y+11)^{5/3}\,\text{d}y.
$$

Now, we let $u=y+11.$ Then differentiating with respect to $y$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}y}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}y=\text{d}u.
$$

We now write our integral in terms of $u,$ calculate the integral as normal, and write the final answer in terms of $u$ at the very end:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (y+11)^{5/3}\,\text{d}y & =\int {u}^{5/3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{{u}^{8/3}}{8/3}+C \\  & =\frac{3}{8}(y+11)^{8/3}+C \\  & =\frac{3}{8}\sqrt[3]{(y+11)^{8}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's double-check that our result is correct. If we differentiate the result, then it should come out to the original integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}[\frac{3}{8}\sqrt[3]{(y+11)^{8}}] & =\frac{3}{8}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}[\sqrt[3]{(y+11)^{8}}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(C) \\  & =\frac{3}{8}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}[(y+11)^{8/3}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(C) \\  & =\frac{3}{8}\cdot \frac{8}{3}(y+11)^{5/3}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y+11)+0 \\  & =(y+11)^{5/3}\cdot 1 \\  & =\sqrt[3]{(y+11)^{5}}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332719 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "1769bd13-d55d-5f6a-9446-919c53c722cf" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-3\operatorname{ln}⁡|2-3x|+C" :db/id 17592186330148} {:answer/id #uuid "54869286-b971-57b4-815f-5bbbdc7c4d50" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-\operatorname{ln}⁡|2-3x|+C" :db/id 17592186330712} {:answer/id #uuid "7f11a40a-6408-5a1b-9034-2e0d3b330be3" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "3\operatorname{ln}⁡|2-3x|+C" :db/id 17592186331071} {:answer/id #uuid "84440df1-9b77-5a93-ac20-596184b2ec9c" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2-3x|+C" :db/id 17592186331124} {:answer/id #uuid "dba89aaa-0aa6-5aba-a139-c4ea916ad0a8" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2-3x|+C" :db/id 17592186331897}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186331897} :answer-field/id #uuid "595a4b0f-ad62-571b-b6da-2d943ad48b26" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332373}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485} :question/id #uuid "2da03267-825e-5f39-863f-d7f53abceed7" :question/math-academy-id "q-49452" :question/problem "$$
\displaystyle \int \frac{1}{2-3x}\,\text{d}x=
$$" :question/worked-solution "First, let $u=2-3x.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-3\,⟹\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u.
$$

We can now rewrite the integral in terms of $u$, solve it, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{2-3x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot (-\frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u) \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2-3x|+C\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332722 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "38ad2ded-1acd-5d0f-9482-ff2d40cddfe8" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-3x-2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+C" :db/id 17592186330459} {:answer/id #uuid "6a0ce5c3-0e37-5bf1-b40e-9f1752a34f46" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{x}^{3}+x+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+C" :db/id 17592186330901} {:answer/id #uuid "7c615908-c6e2-5115-bb4e-9bf4a5d0c8ab" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{x}^{3}-9{x}^{2}+x+\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+C" :db/id 17592186331043} {:answer/id #uuid "9fda2557-86c6-5fb7-959b-9fbd45ed4623" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}+2x-\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+C" :db/id 17592186331387} {:answer/id #uuid "f5494940-6b67-5796-a605-3c01ce2a03d7" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-\frac{9}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}x-3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+C" :db/id 17592186332108}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186330901} :answer-field/id #uuid "78373e7d-b109-554d-afe9-f989789a365a" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332419}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045486} :question/id #uuid "67660e4b-92f2-5ae6-aaa9-23b06f12a0c2" :question/math-academy-id "q-49456" :question/problem "Calculate $$
\displaystyle \int \frac{3{x}^{3}-9{x}^{2}+x-1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x.
$$" :question/worked-solution "We first need to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder parts, which we can do using synthetic division.

We draw up a synthetic division table:

$$
\begin{array}{c|rrrr} & {x}^{3} & {x}^{2} & {x}^{1} & {x}^{0} \\ 3 & 3 & -9 & 1 & -1 \\  & ↓ & 9 & 0 & 3 \\ \hline  & 3 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{array}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\frac{3{x}^{3}-9{x}^{2}+x-1}{x-3}=3{x}^{2}+1+\frac{2}{x-3}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{3}-9{x}^{2}+x-1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x & =\int (3{x}^{2}+1+\frac{2}{x-3})\text{d}x \\  & =3\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x+\int \text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={x}^{3}+x+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+C.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332723 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "0ad15353-0559-5d43-bfe4-8d30e35e2d1d" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-\frac{4}{5}" :db/id 17592186330041} {:answer/id #uuid "0d070b7d-50ab-588a-8479-48734b0e636a" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{3}{2}-2\operatorname{ln}⁡6" :db/id 17592186330066} {:answer/id #uuid "74e6d97d-c3e6-5e34-bba5-c28fe9d5be33" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{5}{2}" :db/id 17592186331000} {:answer/id #uuid "82aae5a3-d878-5d65-b748-fa8008a26efc" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-\frac{1}{2}+3\operatorname{ln}⁡2" :db/id 17592186331104} {:answer/id #uuid "b8bf64f0-a37a-51e7-8438-85fc17e27d9f" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{9}{2}" :db/id 17592186331585}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186331000} :answer-field/id #uuid "dfaa55c2-ac8e-5889-8334-60c285ef9c0f" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332595}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "c1ded718-38aa-5165-9d03-af6b601b4829" :question/math-academy-id "q-49457" :question/problem "Evaluate $$
\displaystyle {\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{x}^{2}+7x+10}{x+5}\,\text{d}x.
$$" :question/worked-solution "We first need to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder parts, which we can do using synthetic division.

We draw up a synthetic division table:

$$
\begin{array}{c|rrr} & {x}^{2} & {x}^{1} & {x}^{0} \\ -5 & 1 & 7 & 10 \\  & ↓ & -5 & -10 \\ \hline  & 1 & 2 & 0\end{array}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+7x+10}{x+5}=x+2.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{x}^{2}+7x+10}{x+5}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(x+2)\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\,\text{d}x+2{\int }_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}{|}_{0}^{1}+2x{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =[\frac{{1}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{0}^{2}}{2}]+2[1-0] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+2 \\  & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332725 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "254e5cf7-471f-50e8-be6a-00fe725a2c42" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "x-\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x-3|+C" :db/id 17592186330269} {:answer/id #uuid "33951d1f-ea38-594d-9f46-2002b6dbb06c" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{x}{2}+\frac{7}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x-3|+C" :db/id 17592186330406} {:answer/id #uuid "b174efff-e3c2-5199-bf28-70379f6c34c8" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{x}{2}-4\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x-3|+C" :db/id 17592186331519} {:answer/id #uuid "c16c5cbe-2009-58f3-9c63-acc020011ec6" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2x-3\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x-3|+C" :db/id 17592186331667} {:answer/id #uuid "f7a19484-5637-5ad4-bd83-dd37bd740e28" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "x+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x-3|+C" :db/id 17592186332124}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186330406} :answer-field/id #uuid "3a8bfb5c-94b5-5347-9440-09e9286e0491" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332299}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "a1457a43-fe5c-5c00-af78-30db339e55cd" :question/math-academy-id "q-49463" :question/problem "Calculate $$
\displaystyle \int \frac{x+2}{2x-3}\,\text{d}x.
$$" :question/worked-solution "First, we pull out the factor of $2$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x+2}{2x-3}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{x+2}{2(x-\frac{3}{2})}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{x+2}{(x-\frac{3}{2})}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

$$
\begin{array}{c|rr} & x & {x}^{0} \\ \frac{3}{2} & 1 & 2 \\  & ↓ & \frac{3}{2} \\ \hline  & 1 & \frac{7}{2}\end{array}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x+2}{(x-\frac{3}{2})} & =1+\frac{\left(\frac{7}{2}\right)}{(x-\frac{3}{2})} \\  & =1+\frac{7}{2(x-\frac{3}{2})} \\  & =1+\frac{7}{2x-3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x+2}{2x-3}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\int (1+\frac{7}{2x-3})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\int \text{d}x+7\int \frac{1}{2x-3}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[x+\frac{7}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x-3|]+C \\  & =\frac{x}{2}+\frac{7}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x-3|+C.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332726 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "338680db-24cd-505d-bb86-f7e20ca84bfe" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "3x-9\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+2|+C" :db/id 17592186330404} {:answer/id #uuid "37b3e49f-6ca8-5bb1-b4c0-459a22bff976" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "x-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+2|+C" :db/id 17592186330446} {:answer/id #uuid "64c0b8af-0611-5474-b601-c4d8f02c186c" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{x}{3}-9\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+2|+C" :db/id 17592186330847} {:answer/id #uuid "6dceecd7-7163-532b-a02a-e72f91ff8016" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "x+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+2|+C" :db/id 17592186330935} {:answer/id #uuid "a3c95368-b6b0-53bc-8846-e7aaa782680e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{x}{3}+\frac{1}{9}\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+2|+C" :db/id 17592186331418}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186331418} :answer-field/id #uuid "92054451-6884-5082-bde2-ac31a363973e" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332455}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "3ea190a7-8ce1-54ef-ac76-4af3dbfd44d8" :question/math-academy-id "q-49465" :question/problem "$$
\displaystyle \int \frac{x+1}{3x+2}\,\text{d}x=
$$" :question/worked-solution "First, we pull out the factor of $3$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x+1}{3x+2}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{x+1}{3(x+\frac{2}{3})}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{x+1}{(x+\frac{2}{3})}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

$$
\begin{array}{c|rr} & x & {x}^{0} \\ -\frac{2}{3} & 1 & 1 \\  & ↓ & -\frac{2}{3} \\ \hline  & 1 & \frac{1}{3}\end{array}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x+1}{(x+\frac{2}{3})} & =1+\frac{\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)}{(x+\frac{2}{3})} \\  & =1+\frac{1}{3(x+\frac{2}{3})} \\  & =1+\frac{1}{3x+2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x+1}{3x+2}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3}\int (1+\frac{1}{3x+2})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\int \text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{3x+2}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[x+\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+2|]+C \\  & =\frac{x}{3}+\frac{1}{9}\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+2|+C.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332729 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "26bff1d2-1a1f-5568-b606-c926ad4e222e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(4x)}{4}+C" :db/id 17592186330288} {:answer/id #uuid "38f382b6-b9e0-5d37-bb15-bf2017958200" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{\operatorname{arctan}⁡(4x)}{4}+C" :db/id 17592186330460} {:answer/id #uuid "88b1a168-dccc-5c24-aa5c-58eef11e4b53" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "4\operatorname{arcsec} (4x)+C" :db/id 17592186331165} {:answer/id #uuid "8a671a08-acf6-51a4-a4b1-a79a1a8a1a19" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{\operatorname{arcsec} (16x)}{2}+C" :db/id 17592186331179} {:answer/id #uuid "c1c62bda-b0cb-5477-843f-9e7f08c270e5" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{\operatorname{arcsec} (4x)}{4}+C" :db/id 17592186331672}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186331672} :answer-field/id #uuid "2ed515ce-b125-59ef-ba87-1982f7680cc3" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332279}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045486} :question/id #uuid "cd302e3c-b39d-509b-8801-010e64d93a57" :question/math-academy-id "q-49519" :question/problem "$$
\displaystyle \int \frac{1}{4|x|\sqrt{16{x}^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x=
$$" :question/worked-solution "Note that we can rewrite this integral as

$$
\int \frac{\text{d}x}{4|x|\sqrt{16{x}^{2}-1}}=\int \frac{\text{d}x}{|4x|\sqrt{(4x)^{2}-1}}.
$$

This integral now resembles the basic one for $\operatorname{arcsec} ,$

$$
\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{{u}^{2}-1}}\text{d}u=\operatorname{arcsec} (u)+C.
$$

The only difference is that instead of $u$ as the variable, we have $4x.$

So, let's substitute $u=4x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=4\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{4}\text{d}u.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{4|x|\sqrt{16{x}^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{|4x|\sqrt{(4x)^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{{u}^{2}-1}}\cdot (\frac{1}{4}\text{d}u) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\int \frac{\text{d}u}{|u|\sqrt{{u}^{2}-1}} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{arcsec} u+C \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{arcsec} (4x)}{4}+C\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332730 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "2ecbc85f-d714-5382-93b4-0d6a65eddbaf" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡\left(K|\frac{3+2x}{3-2x}|\right)" :db/id 17592186330361} {:answer/id #uuid "5d7dd655-f02b-501d-877a-3f2f68ebe7a1" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|(3+2x)(3-2x)|)" :db/id 17592186330782} {:answer/id #uuid "709ffcb8-a0b9-549c-af0a-c14250d3e5d7" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|(3+2x)(3-2x)|)" :db/id 17592186330960} {:answer/id #uuid "7f95e354-c5a0-5520-bc04-04e3b624b88e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-2\operatorname{ln}⁡\left(K|\frac{3+2x}{3-2x}|\right)" :db/id 17592186331075} {:answer/id #uuid "9c30d2a4-3cfe-55c7-9754-70cdeed69842" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2\operatorname{ln}⁡\left(K|\frac{3+2x}{3-2x}|\right)" :db/id 17592186331347}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186330361} :answer-field/id #uuid "d099d8e6-9f09-5bcb-9f4f-b030a1bc2edf" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332565}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045486} :question/id #uuid "7e672d2a-b795-5584-9fd5-3adde760bf8b" :question/math-academy-id "q-49520" :question/problem "Calculate $$
\displaystyle \int (\frac{1}{3+2x}+\frac{1}{3-2x})\,\text{d}x.
$$ Assume that $K$ is an arbitrary positive constant." :question/worked-solution "Let's solve this using the general formula:

$$

$$" :question/worked-solution "First, we rewrite the expression inside the square root:

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{75}{|x+2|\sqrt{(x+2)^{2}-25}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{75}{|x+2|\sqrt{25[((x+2)/5)^{2}-1]}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{75}{|x+2|\cdot \sqrt{25}\cdot \sqrt{((x+2)/5)^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{75}{|x+2|\cdot 5\cdot \sqrt{((x+2)/5)^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{15}{|x+2|\sqrt{((x+2)/5)^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\int \frac{1}{|(x+2)/5|\sqrt{((x+2)/5)^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

This resembles the basic integral for inverse secant:

$$
\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{{u}^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{arcsec} \,u+C
$$

The only difference is that instead of $u$ as the variable, we have $\frac{x+2}{5}.$

So, let's perform the substitution 

$$
u=\frac{x+2}{5}.
$$

Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{5}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=5\,\text{d}u.
$$

Finally, we write the integral in terms of $u,$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{75}{|x+2|\sqrt{(x+2)^{2}-25}}\,\text{d}x & =3\int \frac{1}{|(x+2)/5|\sqrt{((x+2)/5)^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{{u}^{2}-1}}\cdot 5\,\text{d}u \\  & =15\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{{u}^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =15\,\operatorname{arcsec} u+C \\  & =15\,\operatorname{arcsec} \left(\frac{x+2}{5}\right)+C.\end{aligned}

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}{\log }_{4}⁡(x)\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}{\int }_{1}^{e}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}{\int }_{1}^{e}u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}[uv{|}_{1}^{e}-{\int }_{1}^{e}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}[\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)(x){|}_{1}^{e}-{\int }_{1}^{e}x\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}[e\operatorname{ln}⁡(e)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)-{\int }_{1}^{e}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}[e-x{|}_{1}^{e}\,] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}(e-e+1) \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332766 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "6b9d6e3b-4caa-5c28-8e8f-30c7bb36dd87" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "4{e}^{5}+1" :db/id 17592186330916} {:answer/id #uuid "91af4bda-40e5-5609-b9eb-ba605b833593" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "1-4{e}^{-5}" :db/id 17592186331246} {:answer/id #uuid "b0c15c98-6584-5b0a-b607-ad7fc66191d6" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "1-5{e}^{4}" :db/id 17592186331514} {:answer/id #uuid "dafc5ee2-645e-57ed-b348-7496484ddc62" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "5{e}^{-4}+1" :db/id 17592186331888} {:answer/id #uuid "f4073828-309f-5276-8d4a-23b054539de7" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "1-5{e}^{-4}" :db/id 17592186332100}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186332100} :answer-field/id #uuid "7332043f-db6a-5dac-b73f-3e4cc396688d" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332410}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045486} :question/id #uuid "7b3a70c7-8817-5fd3-b793-bb9d93329e57" :question/math-academy-id "q-49716" :question/problem "$$

\displaystyle {\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{2x+6}{{x}^{2}-4}\,\text{d}x.
$$" :question/worked-solution "We'll work out the indefinite integral first and then proceed with the definite integral.

First, we note that a denominator of the integrand can be factored as

$$
{x}^{2}-4=(x-2)(x+2).
$$

So the integrand can be converted into a sum of partial fractions,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2x+6}{{x}^{2}-4} & =\frac{2x+6}{(x-2)(x+2)}=\frac{A}{(x+2)}+\frac{B}{(x-2)},\end{aligned}
$$

which gives

$$
2x+6=A(x-2)+B(x+2).
$$

Plugging in $x=2,$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2(2)+6 & =A(2-2)+B(2+2) \\ 10 & =4B \\ B & =\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, plugging in $x=-2,$ we can eliminate $B$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2(-2)+6 & =A(-2-2)+B(-2+2) \\ 2 & =-4A \\ A & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{2x+6}{{x}^{2}-4}=-\frac{1}{2(x+2)}+\frac{5}{2(x-2)}.
$$

Now, we integrate, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x+6}{{x}^{2}-4}\,\text{d}x & =\int (-\frac{1}{2(x+2)}+\frac{5}{2(x-2)})\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{x+2}\,\text{d}x+\frac{5}{2}\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|(x-2)^{5}|-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+2|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify the result using the laws of logarithms, as follows:

$$

$$

Finally, the definite integral is

\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{2x+6}{{x}^{2}-4}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|\frac{(x-2)^{5}}{x+2}|{|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|-\frac{1}{3}|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|-{3}^{5}|) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{-1})-\operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{5})) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-\operatorname{ln}⁡3-5\operatorname{ln}⁡3) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-6\operatorname{ln}⁡3) \\  & =-3\operatorname{ln}⁡3.\end{aligned}

On the other hand, plugging in $x=-7,$ we can eliminate $B$ and solve for $A:$

$$

$$

$$

which gives

$$
11x+46=A(x+8)+B(x+2).
$$

Plugging in $x=-8,$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}11(-8)+46 & =A(-8+8)+B(-8+2) \\ -42 & =-6B \\ B & =7\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, plugging in $x=-2,$ we can eliminate $B$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}11(-2)+46 & =A(-2+8)+B(-2+2) \\ 24 & =6A \\ A & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{11x+46}{(x+2)(x+8)}=\frac{4}{(x+2)}+\frac{7}{(x+8)}.
$$

Now, we integrate, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{11x+46}{(x+2)(x+8)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{4}{x+2}+\frac{7}{x+8})\text{d}x \\  & =4\int \frac{1}{x+2}\,\text{d}x+7\int \frac{1}{x+8}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+2|+7\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+8|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

            

We can simplify the result using the laws of logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{11x+46}{(x+2)(x+8)}\,\text{d}x & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+2|+7\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+8|+C \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|(x+2)^{4}(x+8)^{7}|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the definite integral is 

$$

$$"} {:db/id 17592186332774 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "4337e381-2a60-5c5c-9308-276258a90336" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "5\operatorname{ln}⁡3" :db/id 17592186330554} {:answer/id #uuid "639dd384-bc8a-5ba4-914e-7b3e50785991" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡5" :db/id 17592186330837} {:answer/id #uuid "85f0701b-e023-56df-926f-7a39fc270845" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2\operatorname{ln}⁡3" :db/id 17592186331139} {:answer/id #uuid "a9341903-3233-5c3a-89b3-545d494844f3" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡2" :db/id 17592186331451} {:answer/id #uuid "afc09428-01ed-5d60-b345-93b553f0092c" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2\operatorname{ln}⁡5" :db/id 17592186331504}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186331451} :answer-field/id #uuid "d06cfba7-b789-5962-80c5-2ed56e573863" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332563}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "74490665-fc5e-5bc9-a392-77f2142c3626" :question/math-academy-id "q-49769" :question/problem "Evaluate $$
\displaystyle {\int }_{-2}^{-1}\frac{x+1}{x(x+3)}\,\text{d}x.
$$" :question/worked-solution "We'll work out the indefinite integral first and then proceed with the definite integral.

First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x+1}{x(x+3)} & =\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{x+3},\end{aligned}
$$

which gives

$$
x+1=A(x+3)+Bx.
$$

Plugging in $x=-3,$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-3+1 & =A(-3+3)+B(-3) \\ -2 & =-3B \\ B & =\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, plugging in $x=0,$ we can eliminate $B$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}0+1 & =A(0+3)+B(0) \\ 1 & =3A \\ A & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{x+1}{x(x+3)}=\frac{1}{3x}+\frac{2}{3(x+3)}.
$$

Now, we integrate, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x+1}{x(x+3)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{3x}+\frac{2}{3(x+3)})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+\frac{2}{3}\int \frac{1}{x+3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+3|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify the result using the laws of logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x+1}{x(x+3)}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+3|+C \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x(x+3)^{2}|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the definite integral is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{-1}\frac{x+1}{x(x+3)}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x(x+3)^{2}|{|}_{-2}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡4-\operatorname{ln}⁡2) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡\left(\frac{4}{2}\right) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡2.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332775 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "2110fc2c-b53c-5662-b67f-f10cc7492150" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{3}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\frac{1}{2x}+\frac{6}{23}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x+3|+C" :db/id 17592186330233} {:answer/id #uuid "5ab0ac59-1c01-5eaa-a40f-d17635c309a6" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{23}{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\frac{1}{x}-\frac{4}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x+3|+C" :db/id 17592186330760} {:answer/id #uuid "5d5b3d4d-5d4c-5be4-bb62-4ed1d026f537" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-\frac{4}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|-\frac{2}{x}+\frac{23}{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x+3|+C" :db/id 17592186330781} {:answer/id #uuid "9e9c1268-b123-56a6-9fae-6ad516e1e630" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\frac{5}{3x}+\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x+3|+C" :db/id 17592186331371} {:answer/id #uuid "cc42d8e8-09ae-5b8b-bc07-34b7995eb0a0" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\frac{23}{6}\frac{1}{x}+\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x+3|+C" :db/id 17592186331762}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186330781} :answer-field/id #uuid "f9f3c0b1-87c5-5322-b17a-eb14d303db5c" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332641}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485} :question/id #uuid "770d90ed-08a8-5022-abd4-286bd91c57b3" :question/math-academy-id "q-49785" :question/problem "Given that

\displaystyle \int \frac{3{x}^{2}+2x+1}{x({x}^{2}+x+1)}\,\text{d}x.
$$" :question/worked-solution "Notice that the quadratic factor in the denominator has a negative discriminant:

$$
D={1}^{2}-4(1)(1)=-3<0
$$

So, we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}+2x+1}{x({x}^{2}+x+1)}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{Bx+C}{{x}^{2}+x+1}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $x({x}^{2}+x+1),$ and we get

$$
3{x}^{2}+2x+1=A({x}^{2}+x+1)+(Bx+C)x.
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=1,B=2,$ and $C=1.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}+2x+1}{x({x}^{2}+x+1)}=\frac{1}{x}+\frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+2x+1}{x({x}^{2}+x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{x}+\frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|.
$$

For the second integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}+x+1.$ Then $\text{d}u=(2x+1)\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int \left(\frac{1}{u}\right)\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+x+1| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+x+1).\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+2x+1}{x({x}^{2}+x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+x+1)+K\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332779 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "0b69188c-717e-584c-a661-6b8e5e7e0408" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{\int }_{-4}^{8}\left(\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}-2\right)\,\text{d}x" :db/id 17592186330048} {:answer/id #uuid "66769022-c347-5623-9bf7-601eac6479c8" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{\int }_{-4}^{8}\left(-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+x+8\right)\,\text{d}x" :db/id 17592186330864} {:answer/id #uuid "7875bea2-4901-5cea-a2aa-26c580173d12" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{\int }_{-4}^{8}\left(\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}-x-8\right)\,\text{d}x" :db/id 17592186331021} {:answer/id #uuid "8b3fdd9d-e5c1-554b-9ea8-a3e1398dab73" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{\int }_{-2}^{4}(x+6)\,\text{d}x" :db/id 17592186331186} {:answer/id #uuid "bb5a57e1-b008-5696-a904-c39d91c01f51" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{\int }_{-2}^{4}({x}^{2}+x+8)\,\text{d}x" :db/id 17592186331601}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186330864} :answer-field/id #uuid "516320ec-66ec-53fb-ade6-09ca7dad40f5" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332349}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485} :question/id #uuid "7be80933-d699-55ea-9666-95ebb475abfe" :question/math-academy-id "q-49880" :question/problem "![](images/1e/1e75b221cacd3d2bad25065fe13bbf77f07fa711fe7f865358ff181039ced560.png)

Which integral gives the area of the finite region bounded by $y=x+6$ and $y=\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}-2$, shown above?

*(Note: Figure not drawn to scale)*" :question/worked-solution "The diagram shows that the intersection points between the two graphs occur when $x=-4$ and $x=8.$ So these will be our limits of integration.

To determine which is the lower function and which is the upper, let's draw our vertical arrow.

![](images/56/56ec4a3e3bd4b8b652832d4b32ba730717a49ab2438ef2c978ea99b291a7f462.png)

The vertical line 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $g(x)=\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}-2,$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $f(x)=x+6.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{-4}^{8}[\,(\text{upper function})-(\text{lower function})\,]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-4}^{8}[\,(x+6)-(\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}-2)\,]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-4}^{8}(-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+x+8)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}

\displaystyle {\int }_{5}^{6}\frac{{x}^{2}-9x+21}{(x-4)^{2}(3-x)}\,\text{d}x.
$$" :question/worked-solution "First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}-9x+21}{(x-4)^{2}(3-x)}=\frac{A}{(x-4)}+\frac{B}{(x-4)^{2}}+\frac{C}{(3-x)}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ $B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x-4)^{2}(3-x)$ and get

$$
{x}^{2}-9x+21=A(x-4)(3-x)+B(3-x)+C(x-4)^{2}.
$$

Plugging in $x=4,$ we can eliminate $A$ and $C$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{4}^{2}-9(4)+21 & =A(4-4)(3-4)+B(3-4)+C(4-4)^{2} \\ 16-36+21 & =B(-1) \\ 1 & =-B \\ B & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=3,$ we can eliminate $A$ and $B$ and solve for $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{2}-9(3)+21 & =A(3-4)(3-3)+B(3-3)+C(3-4)^{2} \\ 9-27+21 & =C{(-1)}^{2} \\ C & =\frac{3}{1} \\ C & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ and substituting the known values of $B$ and $C,$ we can solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{0}^{2}-9(0)+21 & =A(0-4)(3-0)+B(3-0)+C(0-4)^{2} \\ 21 & =-12A+3B+16C \\ 21 & =-12A+3(-1)+16(3) \\ 21 & =-12A+45 \\ 12A & =45-21 \\ A & =\frac{24}{12} \\ A & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}-9x+21}{(x-4)^{2}(3-x)}=\frac{2}{(x-4)}-\frac{1}{(x-4)^{2}}+\frac{3}{(3-x)}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{5}^{6}\frac{{x}^{2}-9x+21}{(x-4)^{2}(3-x)}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{5}^{6}(\frac{2}{(x-4)}-\frac{1}{(x-4)^{2}}+\frac{3}{(3-x)})\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{\int }_{5}^{6}\frac{1}{x-4}\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{5}^{6}\frac{1}{(x-4)^{2}}\,\text{d}x+3{\int }_{5}^{6}\frac{1}{3-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-4|{|}_{5}^{6}+\frac{1}{x-4}{|}_{5}^{6}-3\operatorname{ln}⁡|3-x|{|}_{5}^{6} \\  & =2(\operatorname{ln}⁡|6-4|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|5-4|)+(\frac{1}{6-4}-\frac{1}{5-4})-3(\operatorname{ln}⁡|3-6|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|3-5|) \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\frac{1}{2}-3\operatorname{ln}⁡3+3\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\  & =5\operatorname{ln}⁡2-3\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332784 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "1bb523f6-337d-517c-a2e0-1ae2643cab5e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-2\operatorname{ln}⁡3+6" :db/id 17592186330192} {:answer/id #uuid "475c65c1-db8e-5275-9e24-86f4e13e330a" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-3\operatorname{ln}⁡2-2" :db/id 17592186330593} {:answer/id #uuid "8a7c503b-c042-5870-ab52-c9e84dc594fc" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "4\operatorname{ln}⁡2+4" :db/id 17592186331180} {:answer/id #uuid "9a0ffc0e-686f-5268-9425-c55b0fcb8ffd" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "5\operatorname{ln}⁡5+4" :db/id 17592186331332} {:answer/id #uuid "c8512e2d-a2c6-5eea-98b8-e618ad907ddf" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\operatorname{ln}⁡3-1" :db/id 17592186331722}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186331180} :answer-field/id #uuid "110a7998-6b53-557c-88e4-37cc3407f3a3" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332220}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "e05f40f4-bb40-5adb-aa19-6a15bedeece9" :question/math-academy-id "q-49902" :question/problem "Evaluate $$
\displaystyle {\int }_{3}^{4}\frac{4x}{(x-2)^{2}}\text{d}x.
$$" :question/worked-solution "First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4x}{(x-2)^{2}} & =\frac{A}{(x-2)}+\frac{B}{(x-2)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ and $B,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x-2)^{2}$ and get

$$
4x=A(x-2)+B.
$$

Plugging in $x=2,$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4(2) & =A(2-2)+B \\ 8 & =0+B \\ B & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Now, plugging in $x=0$ and substituting the known value of $B,$ we can solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4(0) & =A(0-2)+B \\ 0 & =-2A+B \\ 0 & =-2A+8 \\ A & =\frac{8}{2} \\ A & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integrand as the partial sum

$$
\frac{4x}{(x-2)^{2}}=\frac{4}{(x-2)}+\frac{8}{(x-2)^{2}}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{4}\frac{4x}{(x-2)^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{3}^{4}(\frac{4}{(x-2)}+\frac{8}{(x-2)^{2}})\,\text{d}x \\  & =4{\int }_{3}^{4}\frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x+8{\int }_{3}^{4}\frac{1}{(x-2)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-2|{|}_{3}^{4}+8\left(-\frac{1}{x-2}\right){|}_{3}^{4} \\  & =4(\operatorname{ln}⁡|4-2|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|3-2|)+8(-\frac{1}{4-2}+\frac{1}{3-2}) \\  & =4(\operatorname{ln}⁡|4-2|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|3-2|)+8\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡2+4.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332785 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "3093957e-b600-549a-aa94-f6eff16fa62b" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "4\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+3|+C" :db/id 17592186330378} {:answer/id #uuid "446fd5ce-d55b-5bca-8c08-7bebb04c4c2c" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+3|+C" :db/id 17592186330564} {:answer/id #uuid "57610450-810b-53cd-b769-0eeb48828a8a" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+3|+C" :db/id 17592186330732} {:answer/id #uuid "990e7f87-f46f-5c57-8462-75c680e07388" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+3|+C" :db/id 17592186331318} {:answer/id #uuid "c40af496-e35d-5592-a703-fa0cf0ade2d3" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "4\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+3|+C" :db/id 17592186331693}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186330378} :answer-field/id #uuid "1bfb35c2-169d-522b-a184-a7dabe1884ff" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332241}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485} :question/id #uuid "6d10b74c-0855-5f3d-9ce9-b42a8bd557bc" :question/math-academy-id "q-49903" :question/problem "$$

$$" :question/worked-solution "First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6x+12}{x(x+3)} & =\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{x+3},\end{aligned}
$$

which gives

$$
6x+12=A(x+3)+Bx.
$$

Plugging in $x=-3,$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}6(-3)+12 & =A(-3+3)+B(-3) \\ -6 & =-3B \\ B & =2\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, plugging in $x=0,$ we can eliminate $B$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}6(0)+12 & =A(0+3)+B(0) \\ 12 & =3A \\ A & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6x+12}{x(x+3)}=\frac{4}{x}+\frac{2}{x+3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{6x+12}{x(x+3)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{4}{x}+\frac{2}{x+3})\text{d}x \\  & =4\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{x+3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+3|+C\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332786 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "8eb71edc-1611-5574-8e7e-8f7b3936ff0e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}" :db/id 17592186331213} {:answer/id #uuid "97f1817a-04e4-55bd-9d46-5de306b15c62" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{3}{2}" :db/id 17592186331304} {:answer/id #uuid "abcc04b6-41a0-58ce-94e2-8537295db75a" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2" :db/id 17592186331475} {:answer/id #uuid "c490eb1b-6330-524a-a5e4-555370670a62" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{5}{2}" :db/id 17592186331697} {:answer/id #uuid "ffc8d2f7-7152-57db-b954-c96f6cb2f941" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{7}{2}" :db/id 17592186332197}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186331697} :answer-field/id #uuid "15871e44-ae83-5585-90d9-a66f6aac88ed" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332228}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "2807863a-263b-547c-96e7-4e784ccb6278" :question/math-academy-id "q-49905" :question/problem "Given that

$$
\int \frac{5x-1}{(x-3)(2x+1)}\,\text{d}x=a\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+b\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x+1|+C,
$$

find the value of $a+b.$" :question/worked-solution "First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$

$$

which gives

$$
5x-1=A(2x+1)+B(x-3).
$$

Plugging in $x=-\frac{1}{2},$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)-1 & =A(2\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)+1)+B(-\frac{1}{2}-3) \\ -\frac{7}{2} & =-\frac{7}{2}B \\ B & =1\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, plugging in $x=3,$ we can eliminate $B$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5(3)-1 & =A(2(3)+1)+B(3-3) \\ 14 & =7A \\ A & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5x-1}{(x-3)(2x+1)}=\frac{2}{x-3}+\frac{1}{2x+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{5x-1}{(x-3)(2x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2}{x-3}+\frac{1}{2x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x+\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{2}{2x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x+1|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $a=2,b=\frac{1}{2},$ and $a+b=2+\frac{1}{2}=\frac{5}{2}.$"} {:db/id 17592186332787 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "1bfc3304-e547-5d93-85cf-d63b46ad634d" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+1|+C" :db/id 17592186330197} {:answer/id #uuid "945ced1f-8fea-5c1d-a75d-ca4b571df7b4" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+1|+C" :db/id 17592186331265} {:answer/id #uuid "b3053017-09aa-5c07-8524-e09690ea6055" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+1|+C" :db/id 17592186331530} {:answer/id #uuid "bf976cda-48d5-50b8-89c7-c7fb49822dfa" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|-2\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+1|+C" :db/id 17592186331648} {:answer/id #uuid "fbc85048-9121-59e1-9a1e-20b6d9412725" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|-3\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+1|+C" :db/id 17592186332163}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186331648} :answer-field/id #uuid "54e3b30d-0abd-511a-a133-4c34869bac9e" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332361}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "b4836967-af93-5f43-b351-fdcfbef30921" :question/math-academy-id "q-49908" :question/problem "$$
\displaystyle \int \frac{2}{3{x}^{2}+x}\,\text{d}x=
$$" :question/worked-solution "First, we note that the denominator of the integrand can be factored as

$$
3{x}^{2}+x=x(3x+1).
$$

We convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{x(3x+1)} & =\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{(3x+1)},\end{aligned}
$$

which gives

$$
2=A(3x+1)+Bx.
$$

Plugging in $x=-\frac{1}{3},$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =A(3\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)+1)+B\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right) \\ 2 & =-\frac{1}{3}B \\ 6 & =-B \\ B & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, plugging in $x=0,$ we can eliminate $B$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =A(3(0)+1)+B(0) \\ 2 & =A\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{x(3x+1)}=\frac{2}{x}-\frac{6}{3x+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2}{x(3x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2}{x}-\frac{6}{3x+1})\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x-2\int \frac{3}{3x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|-2\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+1|+C\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332791 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "000b0a0b-70f8-5315-a3e8-d327557b59b7" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{v}_{\text{max}}=\frac{20}{3}\,\text{m}/\text{s},\,t=2\,\text{s}" :db/id 17592186329951} {:answer/id #uuid "33c26726-2c08-5c56-acf6-11b3a6d892a4" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{v}_{\text{max}}=13\,\text{m}/\text{s},\,t=2\,\text{s}" :db/id 17592186330408} {:answer/id #uuid "354ea829-6b99-586e-9084-20a4da546159" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{v}_{\text{max}}=7\,\text{m}/\text{s},\,t=3\,\text{s}" :db/id 17592186330424} {:answer/id #uuid "638fdc3b-3aeb-5353-bdbb-4803c2a85748" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{v}_{\text{max}}=\frac{29}{3}\,\text{m}/\text{s},\,t=1\,\text{s}" :db/id 17592186330836} {:answer/id #uuid "bea51915-1a2e-5ce4-8e17-178a65bc2f4c" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{v}_{\text{max}}=4\,\text{m}/\text{s},\,t=3\,\text{s}" :db/id 17592186331638}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186330424} :answer-field/id #uuid "ceff4dc0-ec20-5b88-b38d-e75183e810fa" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332561}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "407abfb1-af1c-5ee1-847b-8b98a1270fb4" :question/math-academy-id "q-49950" :question/problem "A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=2-\frac{2}{3}t,$ where $t⩾0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=4\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s},$ calculate the maximum velocity ${v}_{\text{max}}$ of the particle and determine the time when the particle reaches its maximum velocity." :question/worked-solution "The extrema of the velocity $v$ occur at the critical points of $v.$

Since $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=a(t),$ to find the times where $v$ is a maximum, we just need to solve $a(t)=0$ and test each solution using the first or second derivative test.

Solving $a(t)=0$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =0 \\ 2-\frac{2}{3}t & =0 \\ t & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the extremum of the velocity function occurs when $t=3\,\text{s}.$

We now test the extreme value using the second derivative test. For this, we find the second derivative of $v(t)$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}v}{\text{d}{t}^{2}} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\left(\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\right) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(a(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2-\frac{2}{3}t) \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${v}^{″}(3)<0,$ we conclude that the velocity is maximized when $t=3\,\text{s}.$

Now, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2-\frac{2}{3}t)\text{d}t \\  & =2t-\frac{1}{3}{t}^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=4.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2(0)-\frac{1}{3}(0)^{2}+C & =4 \\ 0+0+C & =4\,⟹\,C=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=2t-\frac{1}{3}{t}^{2}+4.$

Finally, we calculate the maximum velocity:

$$
{v}_{\text{max}}=v(3)=2(3)-\frac{1}{3}(3)^{2}+4=7\,\text{m}/\text{s}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332793 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "3543fea0-b938-58c1-bd00-109dd3c70eb2" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-\frac{2}{5}({e}^{\pi }+{e}^{-\pi })" :db/id 17592186330423} {:answer/id #uuid "c52ac36e-14b1-546f-b07f-4bc6d5f7fd0a" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-\frac{1}{5}({e}^{\pi }+{e}^{-\pi })" :db/id 17592186331701} {:answer/id #uuid "e9c7cf65-0dd8-5a3f-a79e-bbb685f2d553" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{e}^{\pi /2}-{e}^{-\pi /2}" :db/id 17592186332002} {:answer/id #uuid "f3c0d314-e8a4-5e16-98e6-8258f95848e0" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{e}^{\pi /2}+{e}^{-\pi /2}" :db/id 17592186332097} {:answer/id #uuid "faf9cf32-eafa-5676-a480-7ce065ad668a" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-{e}^{\pi }-{e}^{-\pi }" :db/id 17592186332155}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186330423} :answer-field/id #uuid "2dfbffea-9b18-5463-a762-458d0fd6ca9b" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332276}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045486} :question/id #uuid "772519fa-1384-5f3f-a9df-50e6d7ec983a" :question/math-academy-id "q-50013" :question/problem "Evaluate $$
\displaystyle {\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{e}^{-2x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x.
$$" :question/worked-solution "Let's denote the indefinite integral by $$
\displaystyle I=\int {e}^{-2x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x.
$$

To use integration by parts, let's suppose that 

$$
\begin{aligned}u={e}^{-2x}\, & ⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-2{e}^{-2x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\, & ⇒\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\int {e}^{-2x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{-2x}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)(-2{e}^{-2x})\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-2x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-2\int {e}^{-2x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-2x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-2J.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we can use integration by parts to evaluate

$$
J=\int {e}^{-2x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x.
$$

To do this, let's suppose that

$$
\begin{aligned}u={e}^{-2x}\, & ⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-2{e}^{-2x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\, & ⇒\,v=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}J & =\int {e}^{-2x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{-2x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-\int (\operatorname{sin}⁡x)(-2{e}^{-2x})\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{-2x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2\int {e}^{-2x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{-2x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2I.\end{aligned}
$$

So, substituting this into our equation for $I,$ we can subsequently solve for $I:$

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =-{e}^{-2x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-2J \\ I & =-{e}^{-2x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-2({e}^{-2x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2I) \\ I & =-{e}^{-2x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-2{e}^{-2x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-4I \\ 5I & =-{e}^{-2x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-2{e}^{-2x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ I & =-\frac{{e}^{-2x}}{5}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate our definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{e}^{-2x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =(-\frac{{e}^{-2x}}{5}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)){|}_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2} \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{-2(\pi /2)}}{5}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right)+\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right))+\frac{{e}^{-2(-\pi /2)}}{5}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(-\frac{\pi }{2}\right)+\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(-\frac{\pi }{2}\right)) \\  & =-\frac{2{e}^{-\pi }}{5}-\frac{2{e}^{\pi }}{5} \\  & =-\frac{2}{5}({e}^{\pi }+{e}^{-\pi })\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332794 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "341bbdfc-0958-57c4-a8fc-adcfd2832b27" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\sqrt{3}" :db/id 17592186330412} {:answer/id #uuid "3a4eb11e-164a-505d-8222-3a3c8cc2aa8e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "4" :db/id 17592186330473} {:answer/id #uuid "5173e85f-be65-57f7-b4ad-50a4243824a9" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "6" :db/id 17592186330686} {:answer/id #uuid "900d9ce2-2884-5941-890f-cca5011570ae" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-8" :db/id 17592186331231} {:answer/id #uuid "e1a39abd-a637-559d-b40e-9331517387e9" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-2" :db/id 17592186331945}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186331945} :answer-field/id #uuid "99a69d51-520e-57bf-a0e9-67ec91b1dca0" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332471}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045486} :question/id #uuid "defadd51-e009-5740-8eb4-1acd4e92eb56" :question/math-academy-id "q-50018" :question/problem "A curve has parametric equations $x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t).$ Given that $$
\displaystyle \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cot}⁡(2t),
$$ calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}$ at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{12}.$" :question/worked-solution "To compute $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}},$ we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)}{\left(\frac{dx}{dt}\right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $$
\displaystyle \frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cot}⁡(2t),
$$ and we can calculate $\frac{dx}{dt}$ as follows:

$$
\frac{dx}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))=-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t).
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cot}⁡(2t))}{-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)} \\  & =\frac{{\csc }^{2}⁡(2t)}{-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}{\csc }^{3}⁡(2t).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate at $t=\frac{\pi }{12},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}{|}_{t=\pi /12} & =-\frac{1}{4}{\csc }^{3}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{12}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{4{\sin }^{3}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{6}\right)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4\cdot {\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)}^{3}} \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332797 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "2738e7d6-3ec2-56da-bb09-17a33c2b70fe" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-\frac{4}{243}" :db/id 17592186330298} {:answer/id #uuid "867fc1cf-c629-5977-a559-5be782a4ae5e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{27}{128}" :db/id 17592186331144} {:answer/id #uuid "9f127cdc-14b6-5ebd-8a6a-cd64704afb31" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{9}{125}" :db/id 17592186331375} {:answer/id #uuid "dec912fa-3516-5bd3-b2f6-ac8182d64e0d" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-\frac{81}{256}" :db/id 17592186331919} {:answer/id #uuid "e88adb0d-e96b-5e45-829e-23733498a044" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-\frac{32}{75}" :db/id 17592186331992}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186330298} :answer-field/id #uuid "d0d8018d-ef9f-5fa9-bbd3-ab865b290ade" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332567}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "3230dff8-85be-5bcf-b6ff-98ca4c7a98c2" :question/math-academy-id "q-50049" :question/problem "Given that 

$$
\frac{x+2}{{x}^{2}(2x+3)}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{C}{2x+3},
$$

where $A$, $B$, and $C$ are real constants, determine the value of $A\cdot B\cdot C.$" :question/worked-solution "Multiplying both sides of the given equality by ${x}^{2}(2x+3)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2 & =Ax(2x+3)+B(2x+3)+C{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=0$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}0+2 & =A(0)(2(0)+3)+B(2(0)+3)+C(0)^{2} \\ 2 & =3B \\ B & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=-\frac{3}{2}$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{2}+2 & =A\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)(2\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)+3)+B(2\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)+3)+C{\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)}^{2} \\ \frac{1}{2} & =C\left(\frac{9}{4}\right) \\ C & =\frac{4}{18} \\ C & =\frac{2}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, letting $x=1$ and using our values for $B$ and $C$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1+2 & =A(1)(2(1)+3)+\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)(2(1)+3)+\left(\frac{2}{9}\right)(1)^{2} \\ 3 & =5A+\frac{10}{3}+\frac{2}{9} \\ 3 & =5A+\frac{32}{9} \\ 5A & =-\frac{5}{9} \\ A & =-\frac{1}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

  

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}A\cdot B\cdot C & =-\frac{1}{9}\cdot \frac{2}{3}\cdot \frac{2}{9} \\  & =-\frac{4}{243}.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332810 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "009b86ae-031b-59f9-9638-98f78b47b2eb" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\left\langle 22,\,\frac{14}{3}\right\rangle " :db/id 17592186329957} {:answer/id #uuid "095132a8-a6ba-5f9b-b804-a0b72756166d" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "⟨25,\,5⟩" :db/id 17592186330028} {:answer/id #uuid "42b0d78f-8192-5ddb-90b5-9ee23fe95cd8" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "⟨27,\,6⟩" :db/id 17592186330546} {:answer/id #uuid "57224302-3dba-59cd-bb50-e576ab2b942f" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "⟨22,\,4⟩" :db/id 17592186330728} {:answer/id #uuid "c7e87bd7-4e87-5312-8ead-58ae1df4adfd" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\left\langle 27,\,\frac{14}{3}\right\rangle " :db/id 17592186331718}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186331718} :answer-field/id #uuid "eb241340-77be-5adc-b966-7053266e143c" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332613}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "c975cf4d-1716-589f-83f8-df6c4aa87765" :question/math-academy-id "q-50200" :question/problem "Evaluate $$
\displaystyle {\int }_{1}^{4}⟨4t-1,\sqrt{t}⟩\,\text{d}t.
$$" :question/worked-solution "To integrate a vector-valued function, we integrate each componentt separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{4}⟨4t-1,\,\sqrt{t}⟩\,\text{d}t & =⟨{\int }_{1}^{4}(4t-1)\,\text{d}t,{\int }_{1}^{4}\sqrt{t}\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨(2{t}^{2}-t){|}_{1}^{4},\,(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{{t}^{3}}){|}_{1}^{4}⟩ \\  & =⟨(2(4)^{2}-4)-(2(1)^{2}-1),\,\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{{4}^{3}}-\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{{1}^{3}}⟩ \\  & =⟨27,\,\frac{14}{3}⟩\end{aligned}

Calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}.$" :question/worked-solution "To find the first derivative, we will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{{y}^{′}(t)}{{x}^{′}(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=6{e}^{3t},\,{y}^{′}(t)=3{e}^{t+2}.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{3{e}^{t+2}}{6{e}^{3t}}=\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2-2t}.
$$

To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)}{\left(\frac{dx}{dt}\right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2-2t})}{6{e}^{3t}} \\  & =\frac{-{e}^{2-2t}}{6{e}^{3t}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{6}{e}^{2-5t}.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332823 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "0533a769-c09b-5be4-b9dd-383bf7fdd72d" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "18" :db/id 17592186330002} {:answer/id #uuid "959d7a81-134b-5300-8906-bbafe1f75ea7" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "8" :db/id 17592186331279} {:answer/id #uuid "c7b69f15-222e-5305-ac1b-e13c42d512c6" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "12" :db/id 17592186331716} {:answer/id #uuid "d2c53d7b-562f-5b44-af6b-2618be9c8d32" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "24" :db/id 17592186331820} {:answer/id #uuid "e1afa523-0468-5a1f-9509-62c941adea9a" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "6" :db/id 17592186331946}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186331946} :answer-field/id #uuid "66b38a8e-f985-5633-8915-563815a052ab" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332392}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485} :question/id #uuid "c4ac61f4-d2e8-54e2-8abe-4c6c436322aa" :question/math-academy-id "q-5047" :question/problem "The function $f(x)$ is defined below. What is the value of 
$$

$$
f(x)=\begin{cases}x+2, & x<1 \\ 3, & x\ge 1\end{cases}
$$" :question/worked-solution "By the additive property of the definite integral, we have

$$

$$"} {:db/id 17592186332840 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "624b7117-00f8-551a-809e-5d1c3ff1debc" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "false" :db/id 17592186467692} {:answer/id #uuid "a1161ac7-f2a2-58a6-8a07-6b82fbac85a4" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "true" :db/id 17592186467693}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186467693} :answer-field/id #uuid "4b52ba51-dd6a-5109-ad4a-86c7ab07785f" :answer-field/key "${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n!}$" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186408166} :db/id 17592186468567} {:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "5a95e3e6-c21e-5dba-88b4-2aa448e29ccd" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "false" :db/id 17592186467694} {:answer/id #uuid "c80a45eb-af40-56af-be7f-df024e54b91d" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "true" :db/id 17592186467695}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186467694} :answer-field/id #uuid "640dfa81-f2e1-5fca-a3e6-abf23e497d33" :answer-field/key "${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{2\sqrt{n}}{n+2}$" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186408166} :db/id 17592186468568} {:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "52924de1-0701-5aac-9b3a-e34d33354697" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "false" :db/id 17592186467696} {:answer/id #uuid "dde7684e-a4ef-50e4-a409-ed9aeefc8f00" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "true" :db/id 17592186467697}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186467696} :answer-field/id #uuid "20a21870-3114-52a9-bdfe-348f688b5b7a" :answer-field/key "${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{n}^{3}}{n+2{n}^{2}}$" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186408166} :db/id 17592186468569}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045486} :question/id #uuid "1a500c68-ffb3-5162-a19f-22fd0f314af1" :question/math-academy-id "q-50971" :question/problem "Which of the following series converge?

Select all that apply." :question/worked-solution "We use the flowchart below to determine which tests to use for each series.

![](images/3a/3aa7f0243efeab51d00aa9694dd018245f7ca4664cc1a5fdf4e646aebb61536e.png)

With that in mind, let's test each series in turn.

- For the first series, we use the alternating series test. Observe that 

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{1}{n!}
$$

is positive and decreasing for all $n\ge 1,$ and ${a}_{n}\to 0$ as $n\to \infty .$ So, by the alternating series test, the series

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n!}
$$

is also convergent.

- For the second series, we use the limit comparison test. Let 

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{2\sqrt{n}}{n+2}\,{b}_{n}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}
$$

Working out the necessary limit, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}L & =\lim_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n}}{{b}_{n}}| \\  & =\lim_{n\to \infty }(\frac{2\sqrt{n}}{n+2}÷\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}) \\  & =\lim_{n\to \infty }(\frac{2\sqrt{n}}{n+2}\cdot \sqrt{n}) \\  & =\lim_{n\to \infty }\left(\frac{2n}{n+2}\right) \\  & =\lim_{n\to \infty }\left(\frac{2}{(1+\frac{2}{n})}\right) \\  & =\frac{2}{1+0} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, $L=2$ is positive and finite. Now, the series

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}
$$

is divergent by the $p$-series test. So, the series 

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{2\sqrt{n}}{n+2}
$$

is also divergent by the limit comparison test.

- For the final series, we use the $n$th term test for divergence. Let 

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{{n}^{3}}{n+2{n}^{2}}
$$

Then, we have $\lim_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n}=\infty ,$ since the polynomial in the numerator grows faster than the polynomial in the denominator. Therefore, by the $n$th term test, the series

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{n}^{3}}{n+2{n}^{2}}
$$

is divergent.

In conclusion, only series $$
\displaystyle {\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n!}
$$ converges."} {:db/id 17592186332848 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "1d794c3d-0f93-5e9b-859b-c340a6282610" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}" :db/id 17592186330206} {:answer/id #uuid "3e2fc078-2b62-5d65-868e-79b45fc7931e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-1" :db/id 17592186330500} {:answer/id #uuid "43112ebc-3e8a-5866-aa5d-6e50c43cc18b" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-\frac{1}{2}" :db/id 17592186330551} {:answer/id #uuid "d79174d3-f14b-59a5-9d4a-8261c63a8d4c" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{4}" :db/id 17592186331855} {:answer/id #uuid "fb6ec74e-8319-5846-b8a1-18ee324765f8" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-\frac{1}{4}" :db/id 17592186332158}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186331855} :answer-field/id #uuid "711e8728-f052-51b4-a0b9-2a8ed9eb7bba" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332407}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "54f3f214-d6dd-5486-9655-fb3920d2f817" :question/math-academy-id "q-51109" :question/problem "$$
\displaystyle {\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x=
$$" :question/worked-solution "We use the identity $$
\displaystyle \operatorname{tan}⁡2x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡2x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡2x},
$$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡2x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this by substitution. Let $u=2x.$ Then $\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u.$ 

Now, we fill the table for the limits of integration, according to the rule $u=2x.$

| $x$ | $0$ | $\frac{\pi }{6}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $\frac{\pi }{3}$ |

Therefore, the integral in terms of the new variable is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{sin}⁡u\cdot \frac{1}{2}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{sin}⁡u\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡u}{2}{|}_{0}^{\pi /3} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{3}\right)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\cdot (\frac{1}{2}-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332849 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "590d6352-1cb2-5f07-b337-1a5ebbae468c" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{3}{8}" :db/id 17592186330748} {:answer/id #uuid "ab5d39fd-d361-5948-ac25-d41727644ddc" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{2}{3}" :db/id 17592186331468} {:answer/id #uuid "b88545d6-ff7b-56de-916f-9ba100472dbe" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{8}" :db/id 17592186331581} {:answer/id #uuid "ea6a7743-731d-57fb-8d43-9d7442d6b434" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{4}" :db/id 17592186332006} {:answer/id #uuid "fa786860-e6f1-53ee-9dfb-09fcd349a209" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}" :db/id 17592186332146}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186331581} :answer-field/id #uuid "18da3dd1-3b0e-5e20-8435-771e2e44e2a5" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332235}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045486} :question/id #uuid "132c7e25-b8d1-5b60-bc80-45357d89a5d1" :question/math-academy-id "q-51126" :question/problem "$$
\displaystyle {\int }_{0}^{\pi /24}({\cos }^{2}⁡2x-{\sin }^{2}⁡2x)\text{d}x=
$$" :question/worked-solution "Here, we use the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta ={\cos }^{2}⁡\theta -{\sin }^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

Letting $\theta =2x,$ we get

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡4x={\cos }^{2}⁡2x-{\sin }^{2}⁡2x.
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /24}({\cos }^{2}⁡2x-{\sin }^{2}⁡2x)\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /24}\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡4x}{4}{|}_{0}^{\pi /24} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\cdot \frac{\pi }{24})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\cdot 0)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{6}\right)-\operatorname{sin}⁡0] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(\frac{1}{2}-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332856 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "04f13677-df0c-5227-8bba-34d6b80ddae4" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "50" :db/id 17592186330000} {:answer/id #uuid "1b9e27b7-7095-5a8b-9710-921e741f0993" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-42" :db/id 17592186330191} {:answer/id #uuid "61a315c1-7847-5d25-940f-454f224005a7" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-56" :db/id 17592186330820} {:answer/id #uuid "625fb442-1570-580f-a661-15a8d06659a4" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "64" :db/id 17592186330832} {:answer/id #uuid "96d16d6e-76a3-5966-8193-677ccf5c270b" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-70" :db/id 17592186331289}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186331289} :answer-field/id #uuid "c619486b-e757-52b4-910a-62ef15d35a5d" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332545}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "a8957bff-2acf-5eaf-99ad-a3f22d63d361" :question/math-academy-id "q-51143" :question/problem "Given that 

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+31}{(x-2)^{2}(2x+1)}=\frac{A}{x-2}+\frac{B}{(x-2)^{2}}+\frac{C}{2x+1},
$$

where $A$, $B$, and $C$ are real constants, determine the value of $A\cdot B\cdot C.$" :question/worked-solution "Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x-2)^{2}(2x+1)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+31 & =A(x-2)(2x+1)+B(2x+1)+C(x-2)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=-\frac{1}{2}$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)}^{2}+31 & =A(-\frac{1}{2}-2)(2[-\frac{1}{2}]+1)+B(2[-\frac{1}{2}]+1)+C{(-\frac{1}{2}-2)}^{2} \\ \frac{1}{4}+31 & =A\left(-\frac{5}{2}\right)(-1+1)+B(-1+1)+C\left(\frac{25}{4}\right) \\ \frac{125}{4} & =\frac{25C}{4} \\ C & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=2$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{2}+31 & =A(2-2)(2\cdot 2+1)+B(2\cdot 2+1)+C(2-2)^{2} \\ 35 & =5B \\ B & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, letting $x=0$ and using our values for $B$ and $C$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{0}^{2}+31 & =A(0-2)(2\cdot 0+1)+7(2\cdot 0+1)+5(0-2)^{2} \\ 31 & =-2A+7+20 \\ 31 & =-2A+27 \\ 2A & =-4 \\ A & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

  

Hence,

$$
A\cdot B\cdot C=(-2)\cdot 7\cdot 5=-70.
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332868 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "00e030aa-17f5-575b-8c19-593762858129" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /3}\sqrt{{\sec }^{2}⁡x+1}\,\text{d}x" :db/id 17592186329960} {:answer/id #uuid "010d087f-2168-5876-808a-6b8533f7c847" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /3}\sqrt{{\cot }^{4}⁡x+1}\,\text{d}x" :db/id 17592186329963} {:answer/id #uuid "1fb829f0-81ef-56be-bafb-8ab19d120737" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /3}\sqrt{{\sin }^{2}⁡x-{\cos }^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x" :db/id 17592186330222} {:answer/id #uuid "26f69ffa-f857-59e2-b56a-7e672ff829bd" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /3}\sqrt{{\cot }^{2}⁡x+1}\,\text{d}x" :db/id 17592186330293} {:answer/id #uuid "6f3c9b4b-592e-55d1-a295-2f8df0fe6364" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /3}\sqrt{1+{\sec }^{4}⁡x}\,\text{d}x" :db/id 17592186330951}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186330951} :answer-field/id #uuid "dec408f1-4e20-5669-b90f-578445063800" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332592}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485} :question/id #uuid "c6b28878-fcf8-5c77-8f92-3c4ca2e564a6" :question/math-academy-id "q-51270" :question/problem "![](images/87/87dc32f8909ac1c05adc981b4133a3f6e721918e4aca6923b08a073d2fb8cfe9.png)

Which of the following gives the length of the curve $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ on $[-\frac{\pi }{4},\frac{\pi }{3}],$ as shown above?" :question/worked-solution "The arc length of a curve $y=f(x)$ between $x=a$ and $x=b$ can be found using the formula

$$
L={\int }_{a}^{b}\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=\operatorname{tan}⁡x,$ $a=-\frac{\pi }{4},$ and $b=\frac{\pi }{3}.$

First, we find the derivative of $f(x):$

$$
{f}^{′}(x)={\sec }^{2}⁡x
$$

Substituting ${f}^{′}(x)={\sec }^{2}⁡x$ into the arc length formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /3}\sqrt{1+{[{f}^{′}(x)]}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /3}\sqrt{1+{\sec }^{4}⁡x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332870 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "0d0374a7-aac2-5b65-b63b-48b09372f6ef" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "v\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right)=⟨-\pi ,\,1⟩" :db/id 17592186330064} {:answer/id #uuid "125bdfb5-0185-5ef4-912f-c54813535009" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "v\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right)=\left\langle \frac{\pi }{2},\,1\right\rangle " :db/id 17592186330107} {:answer/id #uuid "4e619186-79a8-531a-acbe-8d7c8870dff8" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "v\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right)=⟨0,\,0⟩" :db/id 17592186330663} {:answer/id #uuid "5dbe43ae-4302-50f4-aad8-8fc5fdfbea38" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "v\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right)=\left\langle -\frac{\pi }{2},\,1\right\rangle " :db/id 17592186330786} {:answer/id #uuid "a11c9277-e964-5ba1-be5a-ed1dae3ec9dd" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "v\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right)=⟨1,\,-1⟩" :db/id 17592186331399}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186330786} :answer-field/id #uuid "3f3c4445-717d-550d-bf87-b5e255d63938" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332309}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "6043983c-7a93-58b2-8d5d-03f2c93edce1" :question/math-academy-id "q-51321" :question/problem "The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the velocity vector $v$ at time $t=\frac{\pi }{2}.$" :question/worked-solution "The particle's velocity vector is given by the derivative of its position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,1+\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the velocity when $t=\frac{\pi }{2},$ we substitute into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right)-\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right)\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right),1+\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right)⟩ \\  & =⟨0-\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right)(1),1+(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{\pi }{2},\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332872 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "057e127d-c807-591d-8ab4-95e22bc9faaa" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-\frac{2}{5}" :db/id 17592186330004} {:answer/id #uuid "14f48743-4662-5bb5-b53a-426fce87fd5b" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-\frac{9}{22}" :db/id 17592186330117} {:answer/id #uuid "24a5e5b3-07af-51e2-9216-21fb858e7133" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-\frac{3}{10}" :db/id 17592186330262} {:answer/id #uuid "bb79a6c3-0dd4-5153-a975-22a9b4c3f6a4" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{2}{5}" :db/id 17592186331602} {:answer/id #uuid "fe8e9006-4b8f-5722-ab7b-2a091cf005e4" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-\frac{5}{2}" :db/id 17592186332192}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186330004} :answer-field/id #uuid "2e03d404-348d-518f-9017-8816be664314" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332277}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "4bf41725-c484-5d60-bf51-85bf60b6feec" :question/math-academy-id "q-51336" :question/problem "If $x=\frac{2}{y}+\frac{8}{{y}^{2}},$ find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at the point $(3,2).$" :question/worked-solution "First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\frac{2}{y}+\frac{8}{{y}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(2{y}^{-1}+8{y}^{-2}) \\  & =2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-1})+8\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-2}) \\  & =2\cdot (-{y}^{-2})+8\cdot (-2{y}^{-3}) \\  & =-2{y}^{-2}-16{y}^{-3} \\  & =-\frac{2}{{y}^{2}}-\frac{16}{{y}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{-2y-16}{{y}^{3}} \\  & =-\frac{2y+16}{{y}^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y}\right)}^{-1}=-\frac{{y}^{3}}{2y+16}.
$$

Finally, substituting the point $(3,2),$ we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(3,2)} & =-\frac{{2}^{3}}{2(2)+16} \\  & =-\frac{8}{20} \\  & =-\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186332876 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "29a920f7-9f20-5208-9e1d-0c6aab2b18b7" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "r=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-1⟩" :db/id 17592186330318} {:answer/id #uuid "3492e549-cc13-5db4-85c9-4d751fad6572" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "r=⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-2⟩" :db/id 17592186330414} {:answer/id #uuid "41cbb68b-da18-52b9-a043-a839e1494c4c" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "r=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-1⟩" :db/id 17592186330534} {:answer/id #uuid "b67595f7-0643-551e-8f5d-d302ee0b8c53" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "r=⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-1⟩" :db/id 17592186331561} {:answer/id #uuid "f249507b-43e5-55ec-a0bf-fb51853c2209" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "r=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩" :db/id 17592186332080}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186331561} :answer-field/id #uuid "b5e34bfe-fc8c-5d9f-be31-ce6a63c9c697" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186332516}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485} :question/id #uuid "18252347-e352-523e-8b93-4f58594c62c6" :question/math-academy-id "q-51354" :question/problem "The velocity $v$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
v=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩.
$$

Given that the particle is at the position $(0,0)$ when $t=\frac{\pi }{2},$ calculate the position vector of $P$ at time $t.$" :question/worked-solution "To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int \operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t,\,\int \operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{C}_{1},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{C}_{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $r\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right)=⟨0,0⟩.$ Substituting $t=\frac{\pi }{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right) & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right)+{C}_{1},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right)+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨0,0⟩ & =⟨{C}_{1},1+{C}_{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have ${C}_{1}=0$ and ${C}_{2}=-1.$ Therefore, the position vector is

$$
r(t)=⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-1⟩.
